html:
Augusto Pinochet was a Chilean general who led the coup of 1973 and ruled Chile as dictator until 1990. Over 3,000 people were killed or disappeared under his rule, and tens of thousands were tortured.

He made himself president of the junta and used the secret police, the DINA, against the left at home and abroad, through Operation Condor. His economic team, the Chicago Boys, opened Chile to free markets, and after a severe crash in 1982, the economy grew fast.

His constitution of 1980 called for a vote on his rule, and in the plebiscite of 1988 voters said no. He stayed head of the army until 1998. That year he was arrested in London on a Spanish warrant for torture, a landmark for international justice. He died in 2006 without being convicted.
